title: Derived naturality, shifts and site comparison for local-class edges
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Work with ordinary sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A$ on the small etale and pro-etale sites and their ordinary derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and $D^+$ for objects with cohomology vanishing sufficiently far below. Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\tau\in\{\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}\}$, and let $V\in D^+(T_\tau,A)$. Use cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and derived sections at site objects. For each integer $r$, sheafification of $W\mapsto H^r(W,V)$ is canonically $\mathcal H^r(V)$. Its map at the final object defines
$$e_V^r:H^r(T_\tau,V)\longrightarrow\Gamma(T_\tau,\mathcal H^r(V)),$$
which sends a global class to its local classes. For every derived morphism $f:V\to V'$ one has
$$e_{V'}^r\circ H^r(T_\tau,f)=\Gamma(T_\tau,\mathcal H^r(f))\circ e_V^r.$$
Under the canonical cochain shift identifications, $e_{V[1]}^r=e_V^{r+1}$.

For $V\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ let $c_V^r:H^r(T_{\mathrm{et}},V)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^r(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\nu_T^*V)$ be the comparison induced by the derived comparison unit of [sk-prop-sf-comparison]. Under exact inverse image $\mathcal H^r(\nu_T^*V)=\nu_T^*\mathcal H^r(V)$, for every $x$ one has
$$e_{\nu_T^*V}^r(c_V^r(x))=\nu_T^*(e_V^r(x)),$$
where the right side is pullback of the sheaf section using the identification of constant coefficient sheaves. The comparison $c_V^r$ is natural for derived morphisms and compatible with shifts, and the displayed square remains compatible with these operations. No concentration in a single degree or constructibility is required.

proof.text: Work in a universe in which the two site categories are small. On either site the constant $A$-ring sheaf is commutative. The module-sheaf category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. For $V\in D^+$ choose a bounded-below complex $I$ of injective module sheaves with $QI\cong V$, using [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. This complex is K-injective. By [lem-pe-injective-complex-slice-section-model], $H^r(W,V)=H^r(I(W))$ for every site object $W$, with the literal restrictions of $I$ as transition maps, naturally in maps of the representatives. In particular the same formula at the final object computes $H^r(T_\tau,V)$.

source.place: Tag 0BKV, lemma-sheafification-cohomology, resolution model; derived.tex Tags 013K and 070J

proof.text: Let $iI$ be the complex of underlying presheaves of $A$-modules and put $P_I^r(W)=H^r(I(W))$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], presheaf cohomology is computed objectwise and sheafification gives a natural isomorphism $(P_I^r)^\#\cong\mathcal H^r(I)$: termwise sheafification of $iI$ is $I$. The corresponding presheaf map sends a cycle $z\in I^r(W)$ to its image under $Z^rI\to\mathcal H^r(I)$ evaluated at $W$. A boundary maps to zero. Thus, using step 1, its component at the final object is exactly the asserted local-class map $e_V^r$, and its sheafification is the asserted canonical cohomology sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0BKV, lemma-sheafification-cohomology, displayed kernel/image formula and proof; sites-modules.tex lemma-sheafification-exact

proof.text: For $f:V\to V'$ choose injective representatives $I,I'$ as in step 1. The bijection in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents the conjugate of $f$ by a chain map $b:I\to I'$, unique up to homotopy. The naturality assertion of [lem-pe-injective-complex-slice-section-model] computes $H^r(W,f)$ by $[z]\mapsto[b^r_W(z)]$. On cohomology sheaves the same formula follows from [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Hence both sides of the desired naturality equation, evaluated on $[z]$, are the image of $b^r_T(z)$ under $Z^rI'\to\mathcal H^r(I')$. If $b-b'=dh+hd$, their values on a cycle differ by $d(hz)$, a boundary, both for section cohomology and for cohomology sheaves. This proves the equation for every derived morphism and proves independence of representative choices by applying it to their derived isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0BKV, lemma-sheafification-cohomology, cycle formula; derived.tex Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective

proof.text: Use $I[1]$ to represent $V[1]$. It is still a bounded-below complex of injectives. In the cochain convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $(I[1])^r=I^{r+1}$ and $d_{I[1]}=-d_I$. The kernels and image submodules of $-d_I$ equal those of $d_I$. Consequently the same cycle $z$ represents both sides under $H^r(I[1](W))=H^{r+1}(I(W))$ and $\mathcal H^r(I[1])=\mathcal H^{r+1}(I)$. The cycle-to-quotient map of step 2 is unchanged, proving $e_{V[1]}^r=e_V^{r+1}$.

source.place: Tag 0BKV, lemma-sheafification-cohomology, cycle formula; cochain shift convention

proof.text: Now take $I$ on the etale site and write $L=\nu_T^*$, $R=\nu_{T,*}$. The geometric-morphism and fixed-$A$ module adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] makes $L$ exact: it preserves finite limits and, being a left adjoint, finite colimits. The coefficient ring is the same constant $A$ on both sites. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], the canonical identification $\mathcal H^r(LI)=L\mathcal H^r(I)$ respects cycles and quotient maps. Choose a bounded-below injective complex $J$ representing $Q(LI)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the resulting derived isomorphism $Q(LI)\to QJ$ is represented by a chain map $a:LI\to J$. It is a quasi-isomorphism, since its maps on all cohomology sheaves are invertible. Thus $J$ computes the pro-etale derived sections by step 1.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint, exact inverse image case; derived.tex Tags 013K and 070I

proof.text: Identify the specified comparison, rather than choose an arbitrary isomorphism of cohomology groups. By [lem-trf-bounded-below-derived-adjunction] and naturality of the right-derived comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], the derived unit at $QI$ is represented, with target $Q(RJ)$, by the ordinary chain transpose $I\xrightarrow{\eta_I}RLI\xrightarrow{Ra}RJ$. Indeed its unit formula is $\alpha_{LI}Q(\eta_I)$, and naturality gives $RR(Qa)\alpha_{LI}=\alpha_JQ(Ra)$; $\alpha_J$ is invertible because $J$ is termwise injective. Since $L$ is exact, [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] makes $RJ$ termwise injective. At the final object $(RJ)(T)=J(T)$ by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The final-object comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-sections-pushforward] therefore identifies $c_V^r$ with the map on cohomology of the chain map $I(T)\to J(T)$ sending $z$ to $a_T(Lz)$. Here $Lz$ denotes pullback of the section $z$, using $L(A_T)=A_T$. This is an isomorphism by the unit and global-sections assertion of [sk-prop-sf-comparison].

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; canonical comparison unit of sk-prop-sf-comparison

proof.text: Represent $x\in H^r(T_{\mathrm{et}},V)$ by a cycle $z\in I^r(T)$. Step 6 and the definition of the edge show that $e_{\nu_T^*V}^r(c_V^r(x))$ is the quotient class of $a_T^r(Lz)$ in $\Gamma(T,\mathcal H^r(J))$. On the other hand, exactness comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] says that pulling back the quotient class of $z$ gives the quotient class of $Lz$ in $\Gamma(T,L\mathcal H^r(I))=\Gamma(T,\mathcal H^r(LI))$. The cohomology-sheaf isomorphism induced by $a$ sends that class to the quotient class of $a_T^r(Lz)$. This proves the displayed site-comparison square, with precisely the cohomology-sheaf identification in the statement. It does not use surjectivity or injectivity of an edge map.

source.place: Tag 0BKV, lemma-sheafification-cohomology, cycle quotient; exact inverse image case of Tag 07A6

proof.text: For a derived morphism $f:V\to V'$, choose a chain representative $b:I\to I'$ as in step 3 and a chain representative $t:J\to J'$ of $Lf$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], $ta$ and $a'Lb$ are homotopic: both represent the same map $Q(LI)\to QJ'$. Pulling back a section commutes with $b$ by naturality of the ordinary unit in [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Thus the two composite maps defining naturality of $c$ agree on cohomology; the homotopy difference on any cycle is a boundary. The same computation after the quotient maps in step 7 proves naturality of that square. For shifts choose $I[1],J[1],a[1]$. Termwise pullback commutes with this shift because it is additive, and the section map in step 6 becomes the shifted section map. The kernel/image calculation of step 4 identifies its degree-$r$ map with the original degree-$(r+1)$ map, including both quotient maps in step 7. All alternative choices give the same maps by step 3 and the homotopy argument just given. This proves shift compatibility of $c$ and of the square for arbitrary bounded-below $V$.
